properties.statement:
FIVE MORE INSTANCES OF THE AUTHORITATIVE-OBJECT RULE BEING BROKEN, IN ONE SESSION, TWELVE DAYS AFTER A FACT COUNTED FIVE AND WROTE DOWN THE HABIT THAT PREVENTS THEM. 2026-09-04, one agent, one machine. Counted because `fact:five-silent-failures-in-one-session-all-one-shape` (2026-08-23) said 'whether five is a normal rate is unknown' — this is the second sample, and it is also five.

  1. A TEST LOG READ MID-RUN, REPORTED AS FINAL — TWICE. '528 passed across 40 suites', then '1193 across 98', when the truth was 1960 across 185. The output file was written by a grep in a pipeline that lagged the run. The wrong number reached a release commit message and a PR body before being corrected. **This is instance 4 of the 2026-08-23 fact, verbatim, by an agent who had not read that fact.**
  2. `pgrep -f "cargo test"` AS A COMPLETION CHECK — matched the backgrounded SHELL's command line, not a live cargo process, and reported 'still running' nine minutes after the suite had printed its final `Doc-tests` line. The proxy was the wrong object in both directions across the session.
  3. TWO BACKGROUND TASKS KILLED BY THE HARNESS — a workspace suite and a CI watcher — leaving no result. Caught only because the notification said `killed` in as many words.
  4. A BENCHMARK TAKEN UNDER LOAD 3-7 ON 4 CORES made an indexed hydrate read FASTER than an unindexed one. The number was true and measured contention. Caught because the result was impossible, not because anything checked.
  5. `gh pr edit` PRINTED A GraphQL DEPRECATION ERROR AND CHANGED NOTHING, twice. **This is instance 5 of the 2026-08-23 fact, verbatim.** Worked around the same way: `gh api -X PATCH`.

⭐ TWO OF THE FIVE ARE THE SAME TWO THE EARLIER FACT LISTED, AND THAT FACT NAMED THE HABIT THAT PREVENTS THEM: 'read a background task's OWN output rather than the log it is still writing' and 'read back anything you wrote through an API before believing it landed'. The habit was on the record, attached to an ENFORCED rule, for twelve days, and was not consulted at the moment it applied. That is the same finding as `fact:defect-the-commonest-changeevent-mistake-was-fixed-in-the-description-and-a-third-project-hit-it-anyway`, recorded the same day: A RULE WRITTEN DOWN IS NOT A RULE THAT REACHES THE MOMENT.

⭐ THE RULE ITSELF SAYS WHY. Its own text: 'the misreading looks exactly like the answer you wanted. That is why advice was not enough — AGENTS.md already tells agents to read results sceptically, and all four happened anyway.' It also says the rule OWES A DETECTOR and has none, and that 'did you rebuild before you measured' leaves no trace a repository check can see. This session adds: neither does 'did you read the log while it was still being written'.

THE ONE THING THAT WORKED, kept because it is the only countermeasure that did: reading the TERMINATING signal rather than any proxy. `cargo test`'s final `Doc-tests … test result:` line; a task's exit code; a `gh run` `conclusion`; a `gh api` read-back of the body. Every proxy — line count, `pgrep`, elapsed time, a wrapper's exit — failed at least once today.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a detector for the mid-run-read class is possible from the repository. The 2026-08-23 fact's 'cheap habits' are all things an agent does in a shell, and the rule's own note says the build-artifact half leaves no trace. Two samples of five each is still n=2 sessions.
